summary: Ensure every catalog-equivalent runtime module has a valid canonical catalogKey, keep non-catalog modules keyless, and resolve legacy normal versus vine separators by modelFile.

impactAnalysis.notes: Catalog identity becomes an invariant of canonical state construction and project restore. Catalog descriptors resolve a valid key automatically; non-catalog illuminated-foam omits catalogKey. Automatic wall/custom back/auto-depot descriptors therefore receive catalog identity when they correspond to current catalog products. F-013 is directly addressed by including separator modelFile in legacy identity resolution. No dimensions, geometry, placement arithmetic, renderer appearance, BOM classification, or non-catalog module semantics are intentionally changed.

e2e.reason: Catalog identity is persisted state and automatic/catalog construction is browser-visible; Chromium verifies both automatic wall and real catalog-picker persistence carry canonical keys.

risk.notes: The change touches canonical construction and restore identity normalization. Product dimensions and placement behavior are unchanged; the risk is incorrect identity attachment or legacy repair, covered by catalog-wide and browser persistence tests.

migration.notes: No persisted schema version changes. Legacy states are normalized opportunistically on restore: resolvable catalog products gain their canonical key and unresolved/non-catalog states omit the field instead of storing null.

rollback: Revert the catalog identity commits if a runtime module receives an incorrect catalogKey or any legacy project restore regression is observed.
